question: what classes do i need for the bio major besides the bio ones like is physics and calc required
answer:
For the Biology BS, physics is required: PHYS 111 FUNDAMENTALS PHYSICS I LECTURE with PHYS 118L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS I LAB, and PHYS 113 FUNDAMENTALS OF PHYSICS II LECTURE with PHYS 119L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS II LAB. PHYS 116 Physics I with Calculus is not listed in the Biology BS requirements. [1][2]

Calculus itself is not required by name. The math requirement is to select 2 courses from CMPS 147 COMPUTER SCIENCE I; BIOL 354 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS or PSYC 242 STATISTICS; MATH 110 PRECALCULUS; MATH 121 CALCULUS I; MATH 122 CALCULUS II. [1]

Other non-biology requirements include CHEM 117 GENERAL CHEMISTRY II LECTURE and CHEM 117L GENERAL CHEMISTRY II LAB; choose either CHEM 206 and 206L, or CHEM 211 and 211L plus CHEM 213 and 213L, for organic chemistry. The ecology choice may be ENSC 220 THEORETICAL & APPLIED ECOLOGY LECTURE instead of BIOL 221. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS116)

question: how many credits is the math minor and does calc 1 count toward it
answer:
The Mathematics Minor (Minor) lists courses but no total credit count [1]. College minors must include between 16 and 24 credits, including non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits [3]. Its required courses are MATH 122 CALCULUS II; MATH 237 DISCRETE STRUCTURES or MATH 205 MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES; MATH 262 LINEAR ALGEBRA; and one elective from the listed options [1]. MATH 121 CALCULUS I is 4 credits [2], but it is not listed in the Mathematics Minor requirements [1], so it does not count toward the listed requirements.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-MATH) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MATH121) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)

question: what does phys 1 cover is it calc based or algebra based
answer:
Ramapo lists two Physics I lectures:

- PHYS 116 PHYSICS I WITH CALCULUS LECTURE is explicitly the calculus course. It covers Newtonian mechanics, relativity & waves and is the first semester of a two-semester sequence with laboratory. It is 4 credits, carries Gen Ed 18-Scientific Reasoning (GESR), and has this corequisite: “Corequisite Course be enrolled in: - PHYS 116L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS I LAB.” [1] https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS116
- PHYS 111 FUNDAMENTALS PHYSICS I LECTURE covers Newtonian mechanics & waves. It is 4 credits and carries Gen Ed 18-Scientific Reasoning (GESR) and WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT). Its corequisite is “Corequisite Course be enrolled in: - PHYS 118L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS I LAB.” [2] The catalog description does not label PHYS 111 algebra-based. https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS111

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS116) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS111)

question: do i need discrete math before data structures or can i take them at the same time
answer:
The catalog does not list MATH 237 Discrete Structures as a prerequisite for CMPS 231 Data Structures. CMPS 231 requires CMPS 148 Computer Science II, which may be taken concurrently with CMPS 231; it does not say you can take MATH 237 and CMPS 231 concurrently as a pair. [2]

question: whats the difference between the bs in chemistry and the biochem major, like requirements wise
answer:
Both are Bachelor of Science degrees in the School of Science, Nursing, and Health; both require CHEM 117/117L, CHEM 211/211L, CHEM 213/213L, CHEM 324/324L, CHEM 350/350L, MATH 121 and 122, PHYS 116/116L and PHYS 117/117L, plus PATH 001, 002 and 003. [1][2]

Chemistry BS adds CHEM 352/352L, CHEM 427/427L, CHEM 451/451L and MATH 225. It also requires “Select a Minimum of 2 Courses” (6–8 credits) from BIIN 351 Protein Structure and Modeling; CHEM 400 Independent Study: Chemistry; CHEM 421 Advanced Organic Chemistry; CHEM 425 Biochemistry I; CHEM 430 Experimental Biochemistry; CHEM 435 Organic Spectroscopy; CHEM 445 Medicinal Chemistry; CHEM 446 Biochemistry II Lecture; CHEM 450 Special Topics; ENSC 343/343L Environmental Chemistry; PHYS 423 Quantum Mechanics I; SCIN 301, 302 or 401 Research Honors. [1]

Biochemistry instead adds BIOL 111/111L, BIOL 113/113L, BIOL 332/332L and BIOL 407/407L, plus CHEM 425 Biochemistry I, CHEM 430 Experimental Biochemistry and CHEM 446 Biochemistry II Lecture. [2]

Both also publish a Chemistry Minor. [1][2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CHEM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM)

question: how many gen ed credits total do u need to graduate and is there a writing intensive requirement
answer:
Ramapo’s General Education curriculum is ten courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [1]. The catalog says the curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits”; it does not give an exact required total of General Education credits [2]. I don’t have verified information about the exact total for your requirements. The catalog in effect when you matriculated governs your requirements [6].

The pages provided do not state a general writing-intensive requirement for all students. If you have two majors, you must complete all writing-intensive courses required for the second major [13].

For clarification, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [1].
